title: Chicken Breast
summary: Lean poultry cut — America's default weeknight protein since the 1980s.
origins: Chickens were domesticated from red junglefowl in Southeast Asia around 8,000 years ago. Breast meat dominance is modern: selective breeding for fast-growing broilers and diet culture pushed boneless skinless breast to U.S. center plate in the late 20th century.
history: Before industrial farming, older stewing hens and flavorful dark meat ruled home kitchens. Broiler revolution (1940s–60s) made chicken cheaper than beef. Skinless breast became a health-food icon in the 1980s–90s despite being easier to overcook than thighs.
teaching: Dark meat stays juicier — breast needs lower heat or brine 30 min.
Pull at 165°F internal; rest 5 min — carryover cooking finishes the job.
Pound to even thickness before pan-searing — eliminates dry edges.
fun_fact: Dark meat stays juicier than breast because it has more fat and collagen — science, not opinion.
